title: Normalized three-row coefficient diagram and scalar multiplication constraints
statement: Let $\mathcal Y,\mathcal X$ be small sites with module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], sheafified tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and signed direct-sum total complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. A coefficient diagram consists of functors $R_Y,R_X,u^{-1}R_Y$ from $\{0\leq1\leq2\}\times\mathbf N^{op}$ to commutative ring sheaves, a single left-exact inverse-image adjunction, its algebraic inverse images, and a natural ring map $\phi:u^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$. Present the module inverse images by the actual ringed pullbacks [def-pur-cochain-tensor-coherence-data]. Normalized comparisons consist of the natural scalar/pullback isomorphisms $k$ and scalar/tensor isomorphisms $s_X,s_Y$, with the generalized pure-tensor normalizations of [def-pur-cochain-coefficient-arrows]. Their termwise lifts act on arbitrary unbounded cochain complexes. The scalar action unit and scalar composition associator are the left-adjoint-uniqueness isomorphisms conjugate to the identity-on-sections restriction comparisons [def-weil-pbc-system-scalar-coherence]. A semilinear transition is represented by an arbitrary chain map out of scalar extension; square transport uses these canonical scalar associators. The predicates TensorLaws, TensorTransitionLaws, and KappaTransitionLaws record respectively unit/composition equations and commutation with all semilinear transitions. This definition asserts none of those predicates.
